The maker strategy ran on 0x7d67f01d (non-GRID CS2, Dota and LoL, from at least 09-21) and moved to the main account on 10-16, when the main account stopped its GRID taker; it has the same maker prices, feed position and selection on both accounts; in June the same design quoted at the stale public print (0.455 within one tick), and the private value appeared by late September, in the feed era [VALIDATE-only]. [VALIDATE-only] Selection: whole events of non-GRID CS2 / Dota 2 leagues covered by its push-feed product; frozen v5 pooled AUC 0.970 vs activity 0.886, recall 0.74 at lift 3.16, coverage 1.0; its league / GRID component also scores the operator's earlier account's event choice at AUC 0.94 out of sample. [VALIDATE-only] Maker: whole-cent BUY ladders on both outcome tokens (100 shares in CS2, 10 in Dota 2), never sells, merges pairs in a 300-s loop (pair cost 0.978); a burst of n adds takes the n highest free slots V, V - 1c, ..., V - 4c inside [0.05, 0.95] (oracle 0.875 live; confirmed historically through the 5-share accounts). [hypothesis, historical outcome-validated] V is its own in-round win-probability state fed by a private esports push feed: within a round its value drifts toward the eventual round winner (AUC 0.90 vs the print's 0.68), one value per event is written to the map and match books, and the value leads other traders' executed prices (Spearman 0.32 vs 0.15 for other makers). No public source obtained reproduces V to the cent (bookmaker lines, round tables, public game state, filters of prints or book deltas all score at or below the last print). [hypothesis] Taker: FAK buys of the team that gained on messages of the shared push feed (>= 19 subscribers at fixed lags; the operator sat at +30-65 ms behind P4e since late September), taken when its revealed value reaches the stale ask; its maker leg also re-prices at the messages it does not take. Exit: never sells; pulls and re-pairs the complement around its takes; merges complete pairs; holds the residual. Not decoded to the exam bar: the price item needs V to the cent and the outcome item needs the +50-ms take; both stand on a private feed (measured bounds in FINAL_RULE.md). [hypothesis, iteration 14] The private part of V is the push feed's message stream priced at the message: on the feed's clock (informed take clusters) its value steps within 0-3 s and is flat before, the market follows 2-5 s later on those messages (10-45 s on average); a value lagged by even 0.25 s loses the price item (X201), so only the feed itself, not a delayed public source, can carry it.

timing.description: Taker: messages of a shared esports push feed (>= 19 subscribers at fixed lags, 29% of its take clusters co-signed on the same token, 38.5% in any market of the event; P4e 0, 0x2005d16a +25, the wallet +50, three at ~+200, P93 ~+400 ms; lag invariant across event classes within ~10 ms; not shared in football / NBA / tennis), of the plant / turn kind; raw events priced by each subscriber (premium corr with P4e 0.21). Its Dota takes are on the same fan-out (P4e 50 ms earlier on 22% of them; slower co-signers 0xfe8a28be / 0x2529c68d / 0x72aaaaf9 at +450-500 ms). Maker: at its own takes it pulls the complement at +11-19 ms and re-posts after the FAK returns (~1.03 s); between takes it re-prices the ladder without any public trigger (single-order moves in 6 ms, multi-level pulls re-added in ~0.26 s), and these re-pricings precede adverse moves (validated label -0.60c, ground-truth wallet cancels -0.94c in 10 s, other makers' +0.74c); the take hazard rises with them (weak). Not a public execution filter (take vs strip-only AUC 0.52). Iteration 9: the fan-out is one broadcast (order consistency at the marginals' null, common-mode lag residual r 0.86) with a load-dependent slow tier (the trio); the Dota kill messages look machine-timed on isolated kills; the Dota maker bursts are only weakly locked to kills (13% vs 10% within 6 s). Uncensored adds: its informative re-pricings (up on the token / down on the complement) precede 11% of the slower subscribers' takes within 1 s (about 10x the shifted null): the maker leg moves on the feed's messages. Iteration 10 (X136): the maker re-pricing on P4e-alone messages is EVENT-locked (signs before or < 20 ms after the fastest co-receiver maker 0xed446954 on 33% of shared messages, lag corr -0.48; same lag with and without any leader), so it is not a book reaction to a faster maker. Iteration 12: two clocks. Event path (off-tick): takes (0 of 22 on the loop) and triggered actions within a median 17 ms of a book change. Loop path: a free-running ~504-ms loop carries the quiet re-pricings (72.8% of untriggered adds within 15 ms of the predicted tick vs 6% uniform; X158), whose inputs leave a public trace in at most ~14 points of cases. It withdraws whole events for variable lengths (median 12.5 s, 3% at the 3-tick repair) at moments of public action (X159 steps 1-2). The take is consistent with its revealed value reaching the stale ask (X170, AUC 0.81). Event-wide withdrawals start with triggered pulls and end with triggered adds, off the loop (7.8% / 6.2% on tick vs 6% uniform). Iteration 13: the event path is co-reception of a dense hidden stream shared with other operators' makers (65-81% of 'triggered' adds signed before their trigger reached the book; withdrawals start on the same co-mover cluster as other pulls); its maker leg re-prices at the pack's messages it does not take (5.3x shifted), so the take's kind filter sits at the take decision (value threshold), not at its input. Iteration 14 (E3-1, pre-registered, BH on BUILD, VALIDATE confirmation): its maker re-pricing decisions follow the informed takers' signatures (peak +0.4-0.6 s, sign-concordant) and precede public print events by 2.5-5 s; no cross-event synchrony of the unexplained decisions (E7).

price.description: Maker: one private value V per burst plus a mechanical ladder: a burst of n adds takes the n highest free whole-cent slots V .. V - 4c inside [0.05, 0.95], top-first (X163, BUILD-live oracle: set unit 0.875, per order 0.73, up / fresh / down bursts 0.87-0.94; V must be exact to the cent: +-1c gives 0.70 / 0.81, +-2c 0.22 / 0.08). V is not a round-score Markov table (X171: residual 3.22c vs the print's 3.21c), not the others' fresh levels (X153), not SX Bet (X145), not a public per-minute Dota state map (X167 step 1: 0.17 vs the last print 0.42); its quiet re-pricings are sampled on its 504-ms loop with little public trace (X158). Examinable historical anchor: the last print 0.305-0.322 within one tick (VALIDATE); a point-in-time partial-fill book does not beat it (X165, 0.274 vs 0.275). Live: touch 0.42 (fills) / 0.45 (adds). Pre-game 1-2c under Polymarket's print. Iteration 13: V is an in-round win-probability state (its within-round drift predicts the round winner at AUC 0.90 vs the print's 0.68; 0.79 vs 0.62 even 45 s before the print-inferred round end); one value per event written to the map and match books by the same cents (96% direction agreement); not a de-margined BetBoom / SpinBetter / Parimatch Dota line (no closer than the print), not an EMA of prints (<= 0.30), not its own top plus the public delta (<= 0.46 through the machine); the five-slot ladder is confirmed historically through the operator's 5-share accounts (98% of co-bursts inside V - 4c). Iteration 14: the price item tolerates no input lag (X201: a value lagged 0.25 s keeps 0.355 of the set unit, 4 s 0.293; 90% of filled orders are V-change bursts, 0.20-0.23 at any lag); own state transported over the complement and the series map reaches 0.44 (X198; 0.26-0.27 when only on-chain-public own fills are used); on the feed's own clock its value steps at the informed messages (57% / 42% of the 60-s move in (-1, +3] s) with no private pre-message ramp, and the clean print reacts 2-5 s later (X189 first pass). V = map value written into the match book through a series map (slope 0.46).
